title: Borders and icons that follow the text colour
summary: currentColor reuses the color value, so one declaration recolours the whole button.
explanation: currentColor is a keyword meaning "whatever color is on this element". Here the button's border, its dot icon (background-color: currentColor) and its text all follow a single color declaration.
The variants .danger and .success only change color; everything else updates with it. Without currentColor you would repeat each colour three times and risk them drifting apart.
Borders already default to currentColor when you leave the colour out: border: 2px solid uses the text colour.
tryThis: Change color in .danger to #2563eb: border, dot and text all turn blue.
Remove currentColor from the border declaration in .button: it still matches, because that is the default.
Give .dot a fixed background-color: #000: now it no longer follows the variant.
